findings.title: remove() invalidates login caches even when IDP is unknown
findings.body: In remove(), storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) can be null if the alias doesn't exist. registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp) is then called with a null idp, which calls getLoginPredicate().test(null). The predicate starts with Objects::nonNull so it returns false safely, but this relies on implicit behavior rather than an explicit null check, making the code fragile to future predicate reordering and obscuring intent.

findings.title: getForLogin cache key does not depend on organizationId for ORG_ONLY/ALL modes
findings.body: cacheKeyForLogin only incorporates the FetchMode, not the organizationId, but the underlying IdentityProviderListQuery stores results per searchKey (organizationId) within that single cached entry. This means a single invalidation key is shared across all organizationId values for a given mode, which is fine for invalidation but means the cache entry for FetchMode.ORG_ONLY/ALL grows unbounded as more distinct organizationIds are queried (there is no eviction except full invalidation), since IdentityProviderListQuery accumulates entries per searchKey indefinitely until the whole object is invalidated. This can lead to unbounded memory growth in deployments with many organizations repeatedly queried under FetchMode.ALL/ORG_ONLY.

findings.title: update() invalidation ordering depends on stale idpById before delegate update
findings.body: registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate(idpById, model) is called using idpById (the pre-update state fetched via getById, potentially from cache) and the new model, before idpDelegate.update(model) is executed. If getById returned a stale cached entry whose login-eligibility differs from the actual DB state, the invalidation decision could be made on outdated data, potentially skipping a needed cache invalidation when organizationId or other login fields have changed outside of this fetch's visibility (e.g., concurrent updates).

findings.title: getLoginPredicate() missing null-safety for idp.getConfig()
findings.body: The predicate added at line 254 calls idp.getConfig().get(...) without checking if getConfig() can return null. If an IdentityProviderModel exists with a null config map, this will throw a NullPointerException when evaluating login eligibility, breaking getForLogin and all cache paths that rely on this predicate (create, remove, update invalidation logic).
